title: Times Tables: 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10
seo_title: Grade 3 Times Tables Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Multiplication of whole numbers to a total of 100; multiplication tables of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10; use the relationship between multiplication and division.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 3 maths worksheets: the 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 times tables, multiplication and division facts and stories. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 4 × 3 means 4 groups of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12.
  • Order does not matter: 4 × 3 = 3 × 4.
  • The 4 times table is double the 2 times table.
  • Use a multiplication fact to divide: 4 × 3 = 12, so 12 ÷ 3 = 4.

Examples

Example

6 × 4

double 6 × 2 = 12

Answer: 24

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding6 × 4 is not 6 + 4.
One group outCount the groups carefully.
3s and 4s3, 6, 9 … and 4, 8, 12 …

faq.a: Grade R to Grade 3 in South African schools. Grade 3 is the last year; learners are about 8 to 9 years old.
Count in steps and say the facts every day.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: There are 4 groups of 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. 4 × 2 = 8.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: There are 6 groups of 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. 6 × 2 = 12.

items.q: How many counters are there?
How many counters are there?
items.e: There are 3 groups of 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6. 3 × 2 = 6.

items.q: Which matches the picture?
items.e: There are 5 groups with 2 counters in each group: 5 × 2 = 10. 5 + 2 adds the numbers. It does not count the groups.

items.q: Which matches the picture?
items.e: There are 7 groups with 2 counters in each group: 7 × 2 = 14. 7 + 2 adds the numbers. It does not count the groups.

items.q:
Count in 2s. What comes next?
6, 8, 10, ?
items.e: Each number is 2 more than the one before: 10 + 2 = 12. So 2 × 6 = 12.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: There are 3 groups of 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. 3 × 5 = 15.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: There are 6 groups of 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. 6 × 5 = 30.

items.q: Each hand has 5 fingers. How many fingers are there?
items.e: 4 hands of 5 fingers: 5, 10, 15, 20. 4 × 5 = 20. 9 is 4 + 5, which adds instead.

items.q: The red hand is the minute hand. How many minutes past 3 is it?
items.e: The minute hand points to 4. Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. So it is 20 minutes past 3.

items.q: The red hand is the minute hand. How many minutes past 2 is it?
items.e: The minute hand points to 9. Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45. So it is 45 minutes past 2.

items.q:
Count in 5s. What comes next?
15, 20, 25, ?
items.e: Each number is 5 more than the one before: 25 + 5 = 30. So 5 × 6 = 30.

items.q:
Count in 5s. What comes next?
40, 45, 50, ?
items.e: Each number is 5 more than the one before: 50 + 5 = 55. So 5 × 11 = 55.

items.q: How many cubes are there?
items.e: Each rod is 10 cubes. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40. 4 tens = 40.

items.q: How many cubes are there?
items.e: Each rod is 10 cubes. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70. 7 tens = 70.

items.q: How many cubes are there?

Count in 10s. What comes next?
30, 40, 50, ?
items.e: Each number is 10 more than the one before: 50 + 10 = 60. So 10 × 6 = 60.

items.q:
Count in 10s. What comes next?
60, 70, 80, ?
items.e: Each number is 10 more than the one before: 80 + 10 = 90. So 10 × 9 = 90.
9 tens make 90. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90. So the answer is 90.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
How many counters are there altogether?
How many dots are in this array?
items.e: There are 3 rows with 7 dots in each row. 3 × 7 = 21.

items.q: How many dots are in this array?
items.e: There are 3 rows with 9 dots in each row. 3 × 9 = 27.

items.q: Which multiplication matches this array?
items.e: There are 5 rows with 3 dots in each row, so it shows 5 × 3 = 15. 3 × 5 gives the same answer: it is the array turned on its side.

items.q: Which multiplication matches this array?
items.e: There are 4 rows with 3 dots in each row, so it shows 4 × 3 = 12. 3 × 4 gives the same answer: it is the array turned on its side.

items.q:

9, 12, 15, ?
items.e: Each number is 3 more than the one before: 15 + 3 = 18. So 3 × 6 = 18.

items.q:
Count in 3s. What comes next?
21, 24, 27, ?
items.e: Each number is 3 more than the one before: 27 + 3 = 30. So 3 × 10 = 30.

items.q:
Count in 3s. What comes next?
27, 30, 33, ?
items.e: Each number is 3 more than the one before: 33 + 3 = 36. So 3 × 12 = 36.

items.q: Which number is in the 3 times table?
items.e: The 3 times table is 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30, 33, 36. 27 is on the list.

items.q: Which number is not in the 3 times table?
items.e: The 3 times table is 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30, 33, 36. 20 is not on the list.

How many counters are there altogether?
2 × 7 = 14. Double it to find 4 × 7.
2 × 9 = 18. Double it to find 4 × 9.
2 × 12 = 24. Double it to find 4 × 12.

Count in 4s. What comes next?
16, 20, 24, ?
items.e: Each number is 4 more than the one before: 24 + 4 = 28. So 4 × 7 = 28.

items.q:
Count in 4s. What comes next?
28, 32, 36, ?
items.e: Each number is 4 more than the one before: 36 + 4 = 40. So 4 × 10 = 40.

items.q: Which number is in the 4 times table?
Which number is not in the 4 times table?
items.e: The 4 times table is 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40, 44, 48. 26 is not on the list.

items.q: Which is the same as 4 × 6?
items.e: 4 lots of 6 is 2 lots of 6 and 2 more lots of 6: 12 + 12 = 24. The 4 times table is double the 2 times table.

items.q: Which is the same as 4 × 9?
items.e: 4 is double 2, so 4 × 9 is double 2 × 9: 18 + 18 = 36. Double 9 is only 2 × 9.

items.q: A spider has 8 legs. Lerato finds 5 spiders in the garden. How many legs is that altogether?
Yoghurts come in packs of 4. Busisiwe buys 7 packs. How many yoghurts is that?
items.e: 7 packs of 4: 7 × 4 = 28. Double 7 is 14, double 14 is 28.

items.q: In a classroom, 3 children sit at each table. There are 9 tables. How many children are there?
A car has 4 wheels. There are 8 cars in the car park. How many wheels is that?
An octopus has 8 arms. There are 3 octopuses at the aquarium. How many arms is that?
items.e: 3 × 8 = 24. 11 is 3 + 8, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: A chair has 4 legs. How many legs do 9 chairs have?
A soccer team gets 3 points for a win. The team wins 7 games. How many points is that?
Pencils come in packs of 8. Palesa’s teacher buys 6 packs. How many pencils is that?
32 learners get into teams of 4 for PE. How many teams are there?
Lwazi shares 24 cupcakes equally onto 3 plates. How many cupcakes go on each plate?
15 counters are put into groups of 5. How many groups?
items.e: Count the groups: there are 3. 15 ÷ 5 = 3. Check: 3 × 5 = 15.

items.q: Kyle shares 12 strawberries equally between 2 bowls. How many go in each bowl?
items.e: 12 ÷ 2 = ? Half of 12 is 6. Check: 2 × 6 = 12. So 6 strawberries.

items.q: 30 children get into teams of 5 for PE. How many teams are there?
items.e: 30 ÷ 5 = ? Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. That is 6 fives, so 6 teams.

items.q: A bike has 2 wheels. There are 6 bikes in the playground. How many wheels?
items.e: 6 bikes with 2 wheels each: 6 × 2 = 12. 8 is 6 + 2, which adds instead of multiplies.
